findings.evidence: PathCandidate orders by checked u128 distance, then edge count (hops), then the full Vec<EdgeId> lexicographically. The min-heap uses Reverse and stale labels are discarded against best[node]. Every extension adds nonnegative distance and one hop, so label keys strictly increase even over zero-length edges. For a fixed suffix, distance/hop/full-ID order is preserved; unique graph EdgeIds make the full edge sequence identify the path.

Expansion rejects a node already in candidate.nodes. Any nonnegative cycle is dominated by removing it: positive length improves distance and a zero cycle preserves distance while reducing hops. Two internal focused tests cover a zero-cycle/full-sequence tie and dense zero-cost layers; original C20 test also covers zero cycles plus hop preference.

Path and final route distances use checked u128 additions. ceil_ticks checks distance_mm*ticks_per_second before division, then checked-adds the remainder ceiling. Segment offsets use cumulative-distance ceilings, are checked monotone, and the final cumulative offset must equal total duration; zero-length edges can correctly have zero-tick increments.

Nodes are sorted by numeric NodeId; edges by numeric EdgeId; duplicate IDs and invalid references are rejected. Allowed mode IDs are sorted by their exact String ordering and duplicates rejected. Encoding follows the frozen tags/version/unit/counts/IDs/edge fields/mode byte-length/string order using little-endian integers, checked usize-to-u64 lengths, and no profile/runtime values.

The nine frozen C20 cases are present in the original source and runner TEST_NAMES in identical order: validation, duplicates, distance/hops/zero-cycle, full-sequence tie, origin-equals-destination/distinct zero path, permutation/canonical modes, cumulative ceilings, u128 distance, and tick multiplication overflow.
